title: Shortest route, no route-trying
hook: The shortest route seems to need trying every route. A wave finds it without trying one.

knows: moving up, down, left or right one square at a time
doesNotKnow: that labelling cells by distance, nearest first, finds shortest routes

misconception: To find the shortest route you must try every route and compare them.
objective: The learner can explain that growing a wave ring by ring from the start labels each cell with its distance, so the goal's label is the shortest route length, found without listing routes; walls only bend the wave.

claims.text: On an open 5 x 5 grid, opposite corners are 8 steps apart: 4 across and 4 down, in any order.
claims.source: With only up/down/left/right moves, each step changes the row or the column by 1, so the distance is |dx| + |dy| = 4 + 4 = 8, and any order of 4 rights and 4 downs achieves it.

claims.text: Labelling cells ring by ring outward from the start (breadth-first search) gives each reachable cell its shortest distance from the start, with or without walls.
claims.source: CLRS 3rd ed., 22.2, Theorem 22.5: BFS computes shortest-path distances in an unweighted graph. Walls remove vertices; the theorem still applies to the remaining grid.

claims.text: The wave labels each cell once, without trying any route.
claims.source: BFS enqueues each vertex at most once (it is coloured on discovery), so the work is proportional to cells plus links: O(V + E). CLRS 3rd ed., 22.2.

claims.text: On the open 5 x 5 grid there are 70 different shortest corner-to-corner routes.
claims.source: A shortest route is an order of 4 rights and 4 downs: C(8, 4) = 8! / (4! 4!) = 70 (builder computed it in Node).

recall.question: A robot on a city grid wants the fewest blocks to the station. Which plan finds it without listing routes?
options: Mark corners 1 block away, then 2, then 3, until the station is marked
Walk toward the station, turning whenever blocked
Guess a route, then keep improving it
recall.why: Growing outward ring by ring labels each corner with its true distance, so the station's label is the fewest blocks: breadth-first search.
